facts.statement: If the identification of Protoavis as a bird is valid, it would push back the origins of birds by 60 to 75 million years.
facts.quote: When it was first described, the fossils were described as being from a primitive bird which, if the identification is valid, would push back avian origins some 60–75 million years.

facts.statement: The true classification of Protoavis is controversial with many different interpretations of what the animal actually is.
facts.quote: The animal's true classification has been the subject of much controversy, and there are many different interpretations of what the taxon actually is.

facts.statement: Original describer Sankar Chatterjee interpreted the type specimen as a single 35 cm tall bird living in Texas around 210 million years ago.
facts.quote: The original describer of Protoavis texensis, Sankar Chatterjee of Texas Tech University, interpreted the type specimen to have come from a single animal, specifically a 35 cm tall bird that lived in what is now Texas, USA, around 210 million years ago.

facts.statement: Protoavis is reconstructed as a carnivorous bird with front-facing eyes, suggesting a nocturnal or crepuscular lifestyle.
facts.quote: Protoavis has been reconstructed as a carnivorous bird that had teeth on the tip of its jaws and eyes located at the front of the skull, suggesting a nocturnal or crepuscular lifestyle.

facts.statement: Many paleontologists doubt that Protoavis is a bird or that all remains come from a single species due to unconvincing avian features in the fragmentary material.
facts.quote: Many palaeontologists doubt that Protoavis is a bird, or that all remains assigned to it even come from a single species, because of the circumstances of its discovery and unconvincing avian synapomorphies in its fragmentary material.

facts.statement: Protoavis is usually depicted as a bipedal archosaur similar to poposaurids and rauisuchids of the same time period.
facts.quote: Protoavis is usually depicted as being a bipedal archosaur, similar to several poposaurids and rauisuchids that lived during roughly the same time as Protoavis.

facts.statement: The skull has an extremely narrow parietal and very broad, T-shaped frontals that form lateral wings where postorbitals are lacking.
facts.quote: The skull has an extremely narrow parietal with block like dorsal aspect, very broad, T-shaped frontals that form the "lateral wings" that Chatterjee applies to the lack of postorbitals.

facts.statement: Chatterjee presents the skull as complete, though only the rear aspect of the cranium is preserved in available fossils.
facts.quote: Chatterjee presents the skull of Protoavis as complete, although only the caudal aspect of the cranium is represented in the available fossils.

facts.statement: Data suggest that prokinesis in the skull of Protoavis is questionable and that the specimen likely displays a conventional opisthostylic quadrate.
facts.quote: These data render the assertion of prokinesis in the skull of Protoavis questionable at best, and it seems most parsimonious to conclude that the specimen displays a conventional opisthostylic quadrate.

facts.statement: Chatterjee identified the axial skeleton as displaying avian characters including heterocoelous centra, hypapophyses, and reduced neural spines.
facts.quote: Of the postcranial skeleton, Chatterjee has isolated the axial skeleton as displaying a suite of avian characters, including heterocoelous centra, hypapophyses and reduction of the neural spines.

facts.statement: The presence of poorly developed hypapophyses on non-avian vertebrae is regarded as mild convergence rather than evidence of avian affinity.
facts.quote: The presence of incipient hypapophyses in and of itself might be considered indicative of avian affinity, but their poor development and presence on vertebrae otherwise thoroughly non-avian, is most parsimoniously regarded as mild convergence until further material should be brought to light.

facts.statement: Researchers question whether the pectoral girdle features described by Chatterjee were actually present in Protoavis because the fossil preservation is poor.
facts.quote: Chatterjee's interpretation of the fossils identified as such in his reviews of the Protoavis material are open to question due to the preservation quality of the elements

facts.statement: The orientation of the glenoid joint alone is not considered sufficient evidence to classify Protoavis as a bird.
facts.quote: In and of itself, the orientation of the glenoid is not a sufficient basis for placing Protoavis within Aves

facts.statement: The claimed fusion of the ischium and ilium bones in Protoavis is not supported by the available fossil evidence.
facts.quote: The alleged fusion of the ischium and ilium into an ilioischiadic plate is currently not substantiated by the fossils at hand

facts.statement: It is currently impossible to accurately identify specific structures like trochanters and ridges on the Protoavis humerus due to the condition of the fossils.
facts.quote: accurate identification of the elaborate trochanters, ridges, etc., attributed to the humerus by Chatterjee is impossible at this time

facts.statement: The well-preserved wrist and hand bones of Protoavis show features that are distinctly non-avian.
facts.quote: The manus and carpus are among the few areas of the Protoavis material which are well preserved, and they are astonishingly non-avian

facts.statement: Protoavis possesses a fifth metacarpal bone, a feature absent in even the most basal birds like Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: metacarpal V is present

facts.statement: The femur of Protoavis closely resembles that of non-tetanuran theropods such as coelophysoids.
facts.quote: The femur of Protoavis is astonishingly similar to non-tetanurans, namely coelophysoids

facts.statement: Later re-evaluations of the fossil material have failed to conclusively determine if the structures on the arm are true quill knobs.
facts.quote: re-evaluation of the fossil material by subsequent authors such as Lawrence Witmer have been inconclusive regarding whether or not these structures are actual quill knobs

facts.statement: Some structures on the metacarpals that were once thought to be quill knobs may actually be caused by post-mortem damage.
facts.quote: the metacarpal structures appear to be attributable to post-mortem damage

facts.statement: Most paleontologists consider Protoavis to be a chimaera (a mixture of different specimens) rather than an early ancestor of modern birds.
facts.quote: very few palaeornithologists considering it to be an early ancestor of modern birds, and most others in the palaeontological community regard it as a chimaera

facts.statement: Paleontologist Gregory Paul hypothesized that Protoavis is actually a herrerasaur.
facts.quote: American palaeontologist Gregory Paul suggested that Protoavis is a herrerasaur

facts.statement: Almost all paleontologists doubt that Protoavis is a bird or that all its remains belong to a single species.
facts.quote: Almost all palaeontologists doubt that Protoavis is a bird, or that all remains assigned to it even come from a single species

facts.statement: Protoavis fossils were discovered in 1984 at a quarry in the Texas panhandle within a Triassic river delta sedimentary layer.
facts.quote: When they were found at a Dockum Group quarry in the Texas panhandle in 1984, in a sedimentary stratum of a Triassic river delta

facts.statement: Reconstructions depict Protoavis as a carnivorous bird with front-facing eyes, suggesting a nocturnal or crepuscular lifestyle.
facts.quote: Protoavis has been reconstructed as a carnivorous bird that had teeth on the tip of its jaws and eyes located at the front of the skull, suggesting a nocturnal or crepuscular lifestyle

facts.statement: The Protoavis fossils represent a jumbled collection of disarticulated bones resulting from a mass mortality event caused by a flash flood.
facts.quote: the fossils were a jumbled cache of disarticulated bones reflecting an incident of mass mortality following a flash flood

facts.statement: The skull of Protoavis resembles a coelurosaur, but its femur and ankle bone suggest it is related to non-tetanuran theropods.
facts.quote: the pieces of skull appear like those of a coelurosaur, while the femur and ankle bone catalogued under TTU P-9200 and TTU P-9201 respectively suggest affinities to non-tetanuran theropods

facts.statement: Researchers consider the skull and neck of Protoavis to likely belong to a drepanosaurid because they are too large compared to the animal's dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: the entire skull and neck are considered to be most likely from a drepanosaurid because the skull and neck are too big compared to the dorsal vertebrae of Protoavis

facts.statement: Welman argued that the quadrate bone of Protoavis shows shared characteristics specific to theropods.
facts.quote: Welman has argued that the quadrate of Protoavis displays synapomorphies of Theropoda

facts.statement: Gauthier, Rowe, and Dingus argued that the hind limb of Protoavis belongs to a ceratosaur.
facts.quote: Gauthier & Rowe, and Dingus & Rowe have argued convincingly for identifying the hind limb of Protoavis as belonging to a ceratosaur

facts.statement: Feduccia argued that Protoavis was an arboreal thecodont.
facts.quote: Feduccia has argued that Protoavis represents an arboreal "thecodont"

facts.statement: Sterling Nesbitt and colleagues determined that some partial remains of Protoavis belong to a non-tetanuran theropod.
facts.quote: Sterling Nesbitt and others determined some of the partial remains of Protoavis to be a non-tetanuran theropod

facts.statement: Researchers state that the case for Protoavis is currently non-existent, though future material from the Dockum beds might change this view.
facts.quote: While further material from the Dockum beds may vindicate this peculiar archosaur, for the time being, the case for Protoavis is non-existent

facts.statement: Some argue that if Protoavis is valid, it would disprove the theory that birds descended from theropods.
facts.quote: It has been argued that if valid, Protoavis will represent the death knell to the theropod descent of birds

facts.statement: Paleontologists counter that even if Protoavis is valid, it does not disprove the theropod origin of birds.
facts.quote: Palaeontologists counter that if valid, Protoavis in no way falsifies the theropod origin of birds

facts.statement: The holotype and paratype specimens of Protoavis were discovered in the Dockum Group in the panhandle of Texas.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Protoavis (TTU P 9200), the paratype (TTU P 9201), and all referred materials, were discovered in the Dockum Group, from the panhandle of Texas

facts.statement: Protoavis type material was collected in June 1973 and was initially identified as a juvenile Coelophysis bauri.
facts.quote: The type material was collected from mudstone deposits in June 1973 and initially identified as a juvenile Coelophysis bauri

facts.statement: Sankar Chatterjee first described Protoavis and named it Protoavis texensis, meaning "first bird from Texas".
facts.quote: Chatterjee, who first described Protoavis, has assigned the binomial Protoavis texensis ("first bird from Texas") to the small cache of bones, allegedly conspecific

facts.statement: The bone bed where Protoavis was discovered likely resulted from a mass mortality event caused by a flash flood.
facts.quote: The bone bed excavated by Sankar Chatterjee and his students of Texas Tech University, in which Protoavis was discovered, likely reflects an incident of mass mortality following a flash flood

facts.statement: The Dockum Group, where Protoavis fossils were found, dates from the Carnian to the early Norian stages of the terminal Triassic.
facts.quote: The Dockum dates from the Carnian through the early Norian, in the terminal Triassic

facts.statement: The sedimentary layer containing Protoavis fossils was likely deposited in a deltaic river system.
facts.quote: The level of the Dockum group from which the Protoavis material was recovered, was most likely deposited in a deltaic river system

facts.statement: The paleoclimate of the Dockum Group was subtropical with a distinct dry and wet season pattern marked by monsoonal rains.
facts.quote: The inferred palaeoclimate of the Dockum Group would have been subtropical and governed by a distinct dry/wet season pattern, with the latter marked by monsoonal rains

facts.statement: Botanical evidence suggests the area where Protoavis lived was densely forested.
facts.quote: The botanical evidence indicates that the area was densely forested

facts.statement: The principal carnivores in the environment of Protoavis were poposaurids like Postosuchus.
facts.quote: The principal carnivores of the locale would have been poposaurids such as Postosuchus, a species well represented in the Triassic redbeds of Texas

facts.statement: Because only a few parts like a skull and limb bones were found and they do not agree in proportions, many believe the Protoavis fossil is a chimera made of more than one organism.
facts.quote: However, only a few parts were found, primarily a skull and some limb bones which moreover do not well agree in their proportions respective to each other, and this has led many to believe that the Protoavis fossil is chimaeric, made up of more than one organism

facts.statement: The holotype and paratype fossils of Protoavis were found in different locations and were disarticulated and unassociated.
facts.quote: Both the holotype and paratype were recovered from disparate locations, both disarticulated and unassociated.

facts.statement: The Protoavis fossils show significant postmortem damage, with some being so crushed and distorted by geological processes that accurate interpretation is impossible.
facts.quote: The fossils themselves display significant postmortem damage, and are in some cases so badly crushed and distorted at the hand of geological processes, that accurate interpretation thereof is impossible.

facts.statement: In his 1997 book The Rise of Birds, Sankar Chatterjee did not illustrate the actual Protoavis fossils but instead provided artistic reconstructions.
facts.quote: In his definitive analysis of the material, The Rise of Birds (1997), Chatterjee failed to illustrate the Protoavis fossils via pictures or sketches of the fossils proper, and instead offered artistic reconstructions.

facts.statement: The genus Protoavis was originally named by Talbot in 1911 and redefined by Chatterjee in 1984.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Chatterjee, 1984 ; Talbot, 1911

facts.statement: The species Protoavis texensis was described by Chatterjee in 1984.
facts.quote: species_authority: Chatterjee, 1984

facts.statement: Protoavis lived during the Late Triassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Triásico Superior

facts.statement: Protoavis texensis is the only known species of the dubious extinct genus Protoavis, a theropod dinosaur similar to a bird that lived approximately 210 million years ago in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Protoavis texensis («primera ave de Texas») es la única especie conocida del género dudoso extinto Protoavis de dinosaurios terópodo similar a una ave que vivió en el período Triásico, hace aproximadamente 210 millones de años en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Protoavis fossils were found in 1984 in the Tecovas and Bull Canyon formations in Texas within a Late Triassic river delta sedimentary layer, as a disordered pile of disarticulated bones that may reflect a mass mortality event after a sudden flood.
facts.quote: Cuando fueron encontrados en las formaciones Tecovas y Bull Canyon en la península de Texas en 1984, en un estrato sedimentario de un delta de río Triásico, los fósiles eran un alijo desordenado de huesos desarticulados que pueden reflejar un incidente de mortalidad masiva después de una inundación repentina.

facts.statement: Sankar Chatterjee originally interpreted the type specimen of Protoavis texensis as coming from a single animal, specifically a 35-centimeter-tall bird that lived in Texas about 210 million years ago.
facts.quote: El descriptor original de Protoavis texensis, Sankar Chatterjee de la Universidad Tecnológica de Texas, interpretó que el espécimen tipo provenía de un solo animal, específicamente un ave de 35 centímetros de altura que vivió en lo que hoy es Texas, Estados Unidos, hace unos 210 millones de años.

facts.statement: Protoavis has been reconstructed as a carnivorous bird with teeth at the tips of its jaws and eyes located at the front of the skull, suggesting a nocturnal or crepuscular lifestyle.
facts.quote: Protoavis ha sido reconstruido como un ave carnívora que tenía dientes en la punta de sus mandíbulas y ojos ubicados en la parte frontal del cráneo, sugiriendo un estilo de vida nocturno o crepuscular.

facts.statement: Reconstructions generally depict Protoavis with feathers because Chatterjee originally interpreted structures on the arm as quills, the attachment points for flight feathers found in some modern birds and non-avian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Las reconstrucciones generalmente lo representan con plumas, ya que Chatterjee originalmente interpretó que las estructuras en el brazo eran perillas, el punto de unión para las plumas de vuelo que se encuentran en algunas aves modernas y dinosaurios no aviares.

facts.statement: However, subsequent reevaluation of the fossil material by authors such as Lawrence Witmer has not been conclusive regarding whether these structures are real feather quills.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la reevaluación del material fósil por parte de autores posteriores como Lawrence Witmer no ha sido concluyente con respecto a si estas estructuras son o no perillas de plumas reales.

facts.statement: Protoavis is generally represented as a bipedal archosaur, similar to various poposauroids and rauisuchians that lived approximately during the same time as Protoavis.
facts.quote: Protoavis generalmente se representa como un arcosaurio bípedo, similar a varios poposáuridos y rauisúquidos que vivieron aproximadamente durante la misma época que Protoavis.

facts.statement: In a description published by Sankar Chatterjee, certain structures were identified as feather quills, although there has been debate over whether they are actually feather quills.
facts.quote: En una descripción publicada por Sankar Chatterjee, las estructuras se identificaron como pomos de pluma, aunque ha habido un debate sobre si en realidad son pomos de pluma o no.

facts.statement: The braincase of Protoavis is similar in some aspects to Troodon, with an enlarged cerebellum that displaced the optic lobes ventrolaterally, and also has a large floccular lobe.
facts.quote: La caja cerebral de Protoavis es similar en algunos aspectos a Troodon, con un cerebelo agrandado que desplazó los lóbulos ópticos ventrolateralmente, y también tiene un gran lóbulo flocular.

facts.statement: The skull has an extremely narrow parietal with a block-like appearance from above, and very wide frontal bones in a T-shape that form the "lateral wings" that Chatterjee applies to the lack of postorbitals.
facts.quote: El cráneo tiene un parietal extremadamente estrecho con aspecto de bloque desde dorsal, frontales muy anchos en forma de T que forman las "alas laterales" que Chatterjee aplica a la falta de postorbitales.

facts.statement: Chatterjee presents the complete skull of Protoavis, although only the posterior aspect of the skull is represented in the available fossils.
facts.quote: Chatterjee presenta el cráneo de Protoavis completo, aunque solo el aspecto caudal del cráneo está representado en los fósiles disponibles.

facts.statement: From this material, only the roof of the quadrate and orbit, as well as limited portions of the braincase, are preserved with sufficient fidelity to allow a definitive interpretation.
facts.quote: De este material, solo el techo del cuadrado y orbital, además de porciones limitadas de la caja craneana, se conservan con suficiente fidelidad para permitir una interpretación definitiva.

facts.statement: Many paleontologists doubt that Protoavis is a bird, or that all remains assigned to it even come from a single species, due to the circumstances of its discovery and unconvincing avian synapomorphies in its fragmentary material.
facts.quote: Muchos paleontólogos dudan de que Protoavis sea un ave, o que todos los restos que se le asignan incluso provengan de una sola especie, debido a las circunstancias de su descubrimiento y las sinapomorfias aviares poco convincentes en su material fragmentario.

facts.statement: Although it existed much earlier than Archaeopteryx, its skeletal structure is supposedly more similar to that of a bird.
facts.quote: Aunque existió mucho antes que Archaeopteryx, su estructura esquelética es supuestamente más parecida a la de un pájaro.

facts.statement: However, these characters are not robust enough to identify Protoavis as a bird.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estos caracteres no son lo suficientemente robustos para identificar a Protoavis como un pájaro.

facts.statement: The claim that the complete set of tympanic recesses seen in ornithurines are observed similarly in Protoavis is questionable, as the preservation of the braincase is not adequate to allow concrete observations on the matter.
facts.quote: La afirmación de que el complemento completo de los recesos timpánicos que se ven en las orniturinos se observan de manera similar en Protoavis es cuestionable, ya que la preservación de la caja cerebral no es adecuada para permitir observaciones concretas sobre el tema.

facts.statement: The most revealing feature is the total absence of accessory fenestrae in the preorbital fossa, which lead to the maxillary sinuses.
facts.quote: Lo más revelador es la ausencia total de fenestras accesorias en la fosa antorbitaria, que conducen a los senos maxilares.

facts.statement: It has been claimed that Protoavis constitutes the oldest known avian taxon, as its fossils date back about 210 million years, much earlier than those of Archaeopteryx, despite presenting morphological characteristics much more advanced than its younger relative.
facts.quote: Se ha afirmado que Protoavis constituye el taxón más antiguo conocido de un ave, pues sus fósiles se remontan a unos 210 millones de años atrás, mucho antes que los de Archaeopteryx, a pesar de lo cual presenta características morfológicas mucho más avanzadas que las de su pariente más reciente.

facts.statement: Many paleontologists doubt the accuracy of the Protoavis reconstruction.
facts.quote: Muchos paleontólogos dudan de la exactitud de la reconstrucción de Protoavis.

facts.statement: The discovery circumstances in 1984 involved disordered remains scattered chaotically in a sedimentary layer, leading some to suspect it is a chimera built from bones of different individuals.
facts.quote: Las circunstancias de su descubrimiento, en 1984, en el que los restos desordenados se hallaban caóticamente desparramados en un estrato sedimentario, hacen suponer que se trataría de una quimera, es decir, de un ejemplar construido por huesos de distintos individuos.

facts.statement: Discoverer Sankar Chatterjee of the Texas Tech University believed the pile of bone fragments, likely the result of a natural catastrophe like a flood or mud trap, belonged to the same species.
facts.quote: su descubridor, Sankar Chatterjee de la Universidad Tecnológica de Texas, se convenció de que toda la pila de fragmentos óseos —probablemente el resultado de una catástrofe natural, como una inundación o una trampa de lodo— pertenece a la misma especie.

facts.statement: Protoavis is classified within the parent group Theropoda.
facts.quote: Parent group: Theropoda

facts.statement: Protoavis is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Protoavis lived during the Norian stage, from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: The remains of Protoavis were found chaotically scattered in a sedimentary layer.
facts.quote: en el que los restos desordenados se hallaban caóticamente desparramados en un estrato sedimentario

facts.statement: Scientists like Alan Feduccia have cited Protoavis in an attempt to refute the hypothesis that birds evolved from dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Científicos como Alan Feduccia han citado a Protoavis en un intento de refutar la hipótesis de que las aves evolucionaron a partir de los dinosaurios.

facts.statement: The fact that Chatterjee used his purported bird to defend the theropod origin seems to contradict Alan Feduccia's argument that a true Triassic bird would cause the collapse of the theropod dogma.
facts.quote: El mismo hecho de que Chatterjee usara su pájaro putativo para defender el origen del terópodo parece contradecir el argumento de Alan Feduccia de que un pájaro verdadero del Triásico provocaría el colapso del "dogma" del terópodo.

facts.statement: Some parts of Protoavis may be of dromaeosaurid nature.
facts.quote: Esto sugiere que partes de Protoavis pueden ser de naturaleza drepanosáurida.

facts.statement: Gregory Paul noted that the cervical vertebrae of Protoavis and dromaeosaurids are remarkably similar, making them hard to distinguish.
facts.quote: Gregory Paul ha notado que las cervicales de Protoavis y drepanosáuridos son asombrosamente similares, por lo que apenas se distinguen entre sí.

facts.statement: Given the dromaeosaur neck modification for sudden predatory action, superficial similarities in cervical vertebrae between the two taxa are likely just convergent with birds.
facts.quote: Teniendo en cuenta la modificación del cuello del drepanosaurio con fines de depredación por acción brusca, es más probable que las similitudes superficiales en las cervicales de ambos taxones sean de hecho solo convergentes con las Aves.

facts.statement: Chatterjee discusses the pectoral girdle as highly derived in Protoavis, showing synapomorphies of more derived avialans than Archaeopteryx, including a hypocleidium carrying the furcula and a hypertrophied carinate sternum.
facts.quote: La cintura pectoral es discutida por Chatterjee como siendo altamente derivada en Protoavis, mostrando sinapomorfias de avialanos más derivados que Archaeopteryx , incluyendo la presencia de un hypocleidium llevando las furcula, y una hipertrofiado, esternón carinate.

facts.statement: The glenoid appears to be oriented dorsolaterally, allowing a wide range of humeral movement.
facts.quote: El glenoideo parece estar orientado dorsolateralmente permitiendo un amplio rango de movimiento humeral.

facts.statement: Chatterjee claims the pelvic girdle is apomorphic compared to archaic birds, showing a retroverted pubis, fusion of the ischium and ilium, an antitrochanter, and the presence of a renal fossa.
facts.quote: Chatterjee afirma que la cintura pélvica es apomórfica en comparación con las aves arcaicas y muestra un pubis retrovertido, fusión del isquion y el ilion , un antitrocánter y la presencia de una fosa renal.

facts.statement: Reconstructions generally depict Protoavis with feathers, as Chatterjee originally interpreted structures on the arm as quill knobs, the attachment point for flight feathers found in some modern birds and non-avian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Las reconstrucciones generalmente lo representan con plumas, ya que Chatterjee originalmente interpretó que las estructuras en el brazo eran perillas, el punto de unión para las plumas de vuelo que se encuentran en algunas aves modernas y dinosaurios no aviares.

facts.statement: Chatterjee infers the presence of feathers from supposed spike protuberances on the ulna and very crushed metacarpals III and IV, and infers the presence of remige feathers from such structures, though he warns this is uncertain.
facts.quote: Chatterjee infiere la presencia de plumas de supuestas protuberancias de púas en el cúbito y los metacarpianos III y IV muy destrozados , e infiere la presencia de plumas remigias de tales estructuras, aunque advierte que esto es incierto.

facts.statement: The thumb is not medially divergent, unlike the case in all birds.
facts.quote: el pulgar, a diferencia del caso de todas las aves, no es medialmente divergente.

facts.statement: The postcranial remains are so poorly preserved, or worse, than the cranial elements, that Chatterjee's interpretation is in many cases unfounded or speculative.
facts.quote: Los restos poscraneales están tan mal conservados, o peor, que los elementos craneales, y su interpretación de Chatterjee es en muchos casos infundada o especulativa.

facts.statement: The quality of vertebral conservation is poor; while the centra are modified, they do not appear to be truly heterocoelous.
facts.quote: La calidad de conservación de las vértebras es mala. Si bien los centros están modificados, no parecen ser verdaderamente heterocélos.

facts.statement: The reduction of neural spines is questionable.
facts.quote: La reducción de las espinas neurales es cuestionable.

facts.statement: Chatterjee's interpretation of fossils identified as such in his reviews of Protoavis material is open to questioning due to the preservation quality of the elements, and it is currently unclear if any of the characters were actually present in Protoavis.
facts.quote: La interpretación de Chatterjee de los fósiles identificados como tales en sus revisiones del material de Protoavis está abierta a cuestionamientos debido a la calidad de preservación de los elementos y a partir de este momento, no está claro si alguno de los catracteres estaba de hecho presente en Protoavis.

facts.statement: The coracoid, identified by Chatterjee as keeled and retroverted, is, like the supposed furcula and sternum, too poorly preserved to allow precise identification.
facts.quote: El coracoides, identificado por Chatterjee como puntal y retrovertido, está, como la supuesta furcula y el esternón, demasiado mal conservado para permitir una identificación precisa.

facts.statement: The supposed fusion of the ischium and ilium into an ilioischial plate is not currently corroborated by the fossils in question, despite Chatterjee's auspicious illustration to the contrary in "The Rise of Birds".
facts.quote: La supuesta fusión del isquion y el ilion en una placa ilioisquiádica no está actualmente corroborada por los fósiles en cuestión, a pesar de la auspiciosa ilustración de Chatterjee de lo contrario en "The Rise of Birds".

facts.statement: At this time, the pelvic girdle is not well enough preserved to determine if there was or was not a renal fossa, although since no known Mesozoic bird presents a renal fossa, it is unclear why Protoavis should, even if it is more derived than Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: En este momento, la cintura pélvica no está lo suficientemente bien conservada para determinar si había o no una fosa renal, aunque como ninguna ave conocida del Mesozoico presenta una fosa renal, no está claro por qué Protoavis debería, incluso si es más derivado que Archaeopteryx.

facts.statement: The metacarpian structures appear to be attributable to post-mortem damage.
facts.quote: las estructuras metacarpianas parecen ser atribuibles al daño post mortem.

facts.statement: After a more detailed examination of the material, no structures homologous to remige papillae were isolated.
facts.quote: Tras un examen más detenido del material, no se aislaron estructuras que pudieran considerarse homólogas a las papilas remigiales.

facts.statement: It has been argued that if valid, Protoavis would represent the death sentence for the theropod origin of birds.
facts.quote: Se ha argumentado que si es válido, Protoavis representará la sentencia de muerte al origen terópodo de las aves..

facts.statement: Paleontologists reply that, if valid, Protoavis in no way eliminates the theropod origin of birds.

facts.statement: Conversely, its discoverer, Sankar Chatterjee of Texas Tech University, was convinced that the entire pile of bone fragments—probably the result of a natural catastrophe, such as a flood or a mud trap—belongs to the same species.
